slots.title: Brent down 5.4% with US–Iran talks in focus
slots.body:

The US oil ETF $USO closed up 1.1% at $150.01 — a different benchmark than Brent futures.

slots.title: JOLTs and confidence print at 2 p.m. ET
slots.body:
At 2:00 p.m.
ET today, the Labor Department is set to publish JOLTs for August.

Job openings: consensus 7.24 million vs 7.27 million previously.

Quits: consensus 3.00 million vs 3.06 million previously.

The Conference Board’s September consumer confidence reading is due at the same time: consensus 90.0 vs 89.4 in August.

JOLTs counts vacant jobs employers want to fill; quits tracks workers leaving voluntarily.

Which of the three prints matters most for how you read the labor market?

slots.body:

Personal income (month over month): consensus 0.4% vs 0.4% prior.

Core PCE strips out food and energy—the measure the Fed cites when it talks about inflation targets.

slots.title: US cash session — 2026-09-29 close
slots.body:
U.S. stocks closed lower on 2026-09-29.
The S&P 500 finished at 7,683.69, down 0.8% (59.72 points) after a session range of 7,666.60 to 7,724.15.
The Nasdaq Composite ended at 26,820.38, down 0.9%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average at 51,481.51, down 0.7%.
The Russell 2000 closed at 2,817.91, down 0.7%.

The CBOE Volatility Index rose 8.1% to 16.07 from 14.87, with an intraday high of 16.58.
Coverage ahead of and through the close pointed to a continuing Treasury selloff narrative and equity pressure alongside those rate moves; the injected treasury snapshot (dated 2026-09-25) shows the 10-year yield at 5.2% and a 2s10s spread of 0.36.

Sector performance on NASDAQ was led higher by Healthcare, up about 1.1% on average, and Basic Materials, up about 0.8%.
Energy was the weakest group at about -2.5%, followed by Communication Services at about -2.0% and Industrials at about -1.1%.
Technology averaged about -0.3%.

Software and platform names were among the notable meg-cap decliners: Oracle fell 3.3% to 132.63, Microsoft 1.3% to 509.22, and Netflix 2.7% to 69.23, in line with headlines about AI-related disruption fears in software.
Amazon declined 1.4% to 246.15; Alphabet Class A shares fell 0.3% to 342.75 and Class C 0.6% to 339.16.
Apple closed down 0.8% at 338.40.

NVIDIA bucked the broader tech softness, rising 1.7% to 228.86 on heavy activity in the most-actives list.
Taiwan Semiconductor gained 0.5% to 452.88 and ASML rose 1.6% to 1,771.41, while Broadcom slipped 0.9% to 349.57.
Intel, also among the day’s actives, fell 5.7% to 116.03.

Financials showed pressure among large banks: Bank of America declined 2.2% to 55.47.
Visa and Mastercard were roughly flat, up 0.1% to 367.74 and 568.26 respectively.
Johnson & Johnson rose 0.3% to 271.95 and AbbVie gained 0.8% to 266.40, consistent with healthcare’s sector lead.

In energy equities versus crude, Brent crude fell 5.4% to 99.62 while Exxon Mobil rose 1.2% to 162.53.
The United States Oil Fund (USO) closed up 1.1% at 150.01.
Headlines tied the oil complex to U.S.–Iran mediation efforts and export flows from the Middle East.

Cross-asset moves included gold futures roughly unchanged, down 0.1% at 4,163.40.
The dollar-proxy UUP rose 0.3% to 28.70.
Bitcoin slipped 0.4% to 83,130.84.
EUR/USD was about flat at 1.14.

Overseas indexes in the dataset also closed lower: the Nikkei 225 fell 1.2% to 65,098.27 and the Hang Seng fell 1.0% to 24,395.00.
The FTSE 100 edged down 0.1% to 10,684.88.

The economic calendar listed high-impact JOLTs job openings for August, JOLTs quits, and September consumer confidence for release at 14:00 ET on 2026-09-29; the injected bundle does not include those actual prints.
Earnings on the calendar for the date included Carnival and CarMax with estimates only—no reported actuals in the data.

slots.title: Friday: September jobs, 84K expected
slots.body:
Friday, Oct. 2, 12:30 p.m.
ET: September U.S. jobs report.

Headline number to watch: Nonfarm Payrolls — estimate 84K jobs added.

Prior print: 162K (August).

Same release batch:
- Unemployment Rate (Sep): estimate 4.1% (unchanged vs prior 4.1%)
- Average Hourly Earnings YoY: estimate 3.1%
- Private payrolls: estimate 85K vs prior 127K

The report counts hiring across the economy and is one of the main monthly checks on labor demand.

It lands after ADP (Wed.) and weekly jobless claims (Thu.) in the same week.

Which line in the report do you track first — payrolls, unemployment, or wages?
